topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.21(a), what standard must a broker's supervision of an associated salesperson meet with respect to the general real estate brokerage business?
choice_a: Regular, frequent, and consistent personal guidance, instruction, oversight, and superintendence
choice_b: Occasional review of the salesperson's closed transactions only
choice_c: Annual written performance evaluations
choice_d: Supervision delegated entirely to an office manager without broker involvement
explanation: 19 NYCRR 175.21(a) defines the supervision required by RPL 441(1)(d) as regular, frequent, and consistent personal guidance, instruction, oversight, and superintendence by the broker.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: For purposes of broker-license qualifying experience, 19 NYCRR 175.21(c) defines "active participation" in the general real estate brokerage business as active service under a licensed broker's supervision for at least:
choice_a: 20 hours per week for 40 weeks per year
choice_b: 35 hours per week for 50 weeks in each qualifying year
choice_c: 40 hours per week for 52 weeks per year
choice_d: 30 hours per week for 48 weeks per year
explanation: 175.21(c) sets "active participation" at at least 35 hours per week for 50 weeks in each qualifying year.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: According to 19 NYCRR 175.21(b), what must a broker and an associated salesperson maintain regarding the salesperson's listings and transactions?
choice_a: No records are required if the salesperson is compensated on commission only
choice_b: Records maintained solely by the salesperson, never shared with the broker
choice_c: Written records sufficient to clearly identify the transactions and their dates, to be submitted to DOS with a later broker-license application
choice_d: Verbal weekly progress reports made directly to DOS
explanation: 175.21(b) requires written records of all listings obtained by, and sales/transactions effected by or with the assistance of, the salesperson, sufficient to clearly identify the transactions and dates, submitted to DOS with a later broker-license application.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.20(a), a branch office may be owned, maintained, and operated only by:
choice_a: Any employee designated by the broker
choice_b: A committee of associated salespersons
choice_c: The salesperson who generates the most business at that location
choice_d: The licensed broker to whom the branch office license was issued; a salesperson may not pay for or be responsible for branch expenses or otherwise operate it for their own benefit
explanation: 175.20(a) restricts branch office ownership/operation to the licensed broker holding the branch license, and prohibits structuring the branch so a salesperson or employee bears its expenses or operates it for their own benefit.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Per 19 NYCRR 175.20(b), every branch office must be under the direct supervision of:
choice_a: The licensed broker or a representative broker of the corporation/partnership holding the license
choice_b: Any salesperson with at least 2 years' experience
choice_c: A part-time consultant hired for that purpose
choice_d: No supervision is required if the branch has fewer than 3 licensees
explanation: 175.20(b) requires every branch office to be under the direct supervision of the licensed broker or a representative broker of a corporation/partnership holding the license.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.20(d), before a broker may relocate a principal office or a branch office, the broker must:
choice_a: Notify DOS within 30 days after the move
choice_b: Obtain DOS's prior approval
choice_c: File a notice with the county clerk only
choice_d: No approval or notice is required for moves within the same city
explanation: 175.20(d) prohibits a broker from relocating a principal office or branch office without DOS's prior approval.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.22, a licensed salesperson associated with a real estate brokerage corporation is prohibited from:
choice_a: Owning non-voting preferred stock in the corporation
choice_b: Serving as a corporate officer
choice_c: Owning, singly or jointly, directly or indirectly, any voting shares of stock in the licensed brokerage corporation with which the salesperson is associated
choice_d: Receiving a year-end bonus from the corporation
explanation: 175.22 flatly prohibits a licensed salesperson from owning any voting stock, singly or jointly, directly or indirectly, in the brokerage corporation with which they are associated.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Per 19 NYCRR 175.23(a), how long must a licensed broker keep records of each residential real property transaction handled through the broker's office?
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 2 years
choice_c: 5 years
choice_d: 3 years
explanation: 175.23(a) requires brokers to keep transaction records for residential real property sales for 3 years.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.13, a broker may not accept the services of another broker's salesperson or employee, or give/offer anything of value to influence or reward that person's actions, without:
choice_a: The knowledge of that salesperson's own employing/sponsoring broker
choice_b: Written pre-approval from DOS
choice_c: A signed release from the salesperson only
choice_d: Nothing is required; brokers may freely use any salesperson's services
explanation: 175.13 requires the knowledge of the salesperson's/employee's own broker before another broker may accept their services or give anything of value to influence/reward their actions.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Per 19 NYCRR 175.14, upon terminating association with a broker, a salesperson must:
choice_a: Retain all listing information as personal property
choice_b: Forthwith turn over to the broker all listing information obtained during the association, whether originally given by the broker, copied from broker records, or independently acquired
choice_c: Destroy all listing records to protect client confidentiality
choice_d: Provide the listing information only if separately compensated for it
explanation: 175.14 requires a salesperson, upon termination of association, to forthwith turn over to the broker all listing information obtained during the association, regardless of its source.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.18, DOS may deny a broker's (or applicant's) use of a trade or corporate name if:
choice_a: The name includes a national franchise brand
choice_b: The name includes the broker's own surname
choice_c: The name is, in DOS's opinion, so similar to another licensed broker's name that public confusion would result
choice_d: The name exceeds 30 characters
explanation: 175.18 prohibits a broker from using a trade or corporate name so similar to another licensed broker's name that, in DOS's opinion, public confusion would result.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(b)(1), who may place or cause the publication of an advertisement for the sale or lease of real property?
choice_a: Any licensed salesperson, without restriction
choice_b: Only unlicensed marketing staff hired by the brokerage
choice_c: Only the property owner directly
choice_d: Only a real estate broker; an associate broker, salesperson, or team may advertise only property listed with or represented by their own sponsoring broker, with that broker's approval
explanation: 175.25(b)(1) reserves the right to place ads to the real estate broker; associated licensees/teams may advertise only their own sponsoring broker's listings, and only with that broker's approval.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Which of the following license-type descriptors is expressly PROHIBITED in advertising under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(4)?
choice_a: "Sales associate"
choice_b: "Real estate salesperson"
choice_c: "Associate real estate broker"
choice_d: "Real estate broker"
explanation: 175.25(c)(4) requires ads to correctly state license type and specifically prohibits the titles "sales associate," "licensed sales agent," or simply "broker" as license-type descriptors.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: If a licensee advertises under a nickname, 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(3) requires that:
choice_a: DOS pre-approve the nickname in writing
choice_b: The licensee's full DOS-licensed name must also appear clearly and conspicuously in the advertisement
choice_c: The nickname be registered as a trade name
choice_d: Nicknames may never be used in real estate advertising
explanation: 175.25(c)(3) requires licensees to advertise under their DOS-licensed name, but permits a nickname if the full licensed name also appears clearly and conspicuously.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(10), a real estate advertisement may NOT:
choice_a: Overstate the property's square footage
choice_b: Omit an MLS listing number
choice_c: Guarantee future profits from real estate activity
choice_d: Include a licensee's professional headshot
explanation: 175.25(c)(10) prohibits advertisements from guaranteeing future profits from any real estate activity.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Per 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(5), any sign placed on listed property must:
choice_a: State the seller's confidential reserve price
choice_b: Be removed within 24 hours of any offer being made
choice_c: Include only the salesperson's personal cell number
choice_d: Identify the representative broker or brokerage
explanation: 175.25(d)(5) requires that any sign on listed property identify the representative broker/brokerage.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(e)(1), a real estate team's advertised name must include the word "team," and may NOT include which of the following terms?
choice_a: "Group"
choice_b: The full licensed names of the team's members
choice_c: "at [broker/brokerage name]"
choice_d: "of [broker/brokerage name]"
explanation: 175.25(e)(1) requires team names to use the word "team" and prohibits terms like "associates," "realty," or "group"; a team name must either include full licensed names or be followed by "at/of [broker/brokerage name]."

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Per 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(2), a licensee's business card must contain:
choice_a: Only the licensee's name and personal email address
choice_b: Business address, license type, sponsoring broker/brokerage name, and office telephone number
choice_c: A complete list of the licensee's current listings
choice_d: The licensee's home address
explanation: 175.25(d)(2) requires business cards to contain the business address, license type, sponsoring broker/brokerage name, and office telephone number.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.26, if a broker conducts business from an apartment building where lobby sign-posting is not permitted by building rules, the required business sign must instead be posted:
choice_a: In the building's mailroom
choice_b: On the building's exterior facing the street
choice_c: On the corridor wall next to (or on) the entrance door of the dwelling unit where the business is conducted
choice_d: No sign is required in that circumstance
explanation: 175.26 requires the RPL 441-a(3) business sign to be posted on the corridor wall next to (or on) the entrance door of the dwelling unit where the business is conducted, when lobby posting isn't permitted.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: For a license renewal period commencing after November 1, 1995, how many hours of DOS-approved continuing education must a licensee complete within the preceding 2 years for renewal?
choice_a: 15 hours
choice_b: 18 hours
choice_c: 20 hours
choice_d: 22.5 hours
explanation: RPL 441(3)(a) and 19 NYCRR 177.1(a) require 22.5 hours of DOS-approved continuing education within the 2 years preceding renewal, including specified minimum hours in cultural competency, fair housing, implicit bias, ethics, legal developments, and agency.
